name: Courtyard by Marriott Singapore Novena
short_description: A select-service Courtyard on Irrawaddy Road in the Novena medical and residential district.
ai_summary: Courtyard by Marriott Singapore Novena sits on Irrawaddy Road in the Novena district, known for its cluster of private hospitals and medical centers as well as residential neighborhoods, and is built directly on top of Novena MRT station. Guest reviews consistently praise the transit-connected location, a 33rd-floor infinity pool with city views, and a well-regarded weekday evening reception with drinks and light snacks. As a select-service Courtyard, it's positioned for value-conscious business and medical-tourism travelers rather than the leisure or convention-district crowd the downtown hotels target. The most common complaints are about value trade-offs rather than quality: standard rooms are described as small even at the premium tier, breakfast is a paid add-on at roughly SGD 35 (free only for Titanium Elite and above), and at least one review noted the pool deck was closed for renovation during a stay.

elite_benefits: Room upgrades for Platinum Elite and above, subject to availability (select-service upgrade pool)
Bonus points in lieu of breakfast for Platinum Elite and above at hotels without full breakfast service
Enhanced Wi-Fi and a welcome amenity for all Elite tiers

pros: Built directly on top of Novena MRT station, close to Novena's private hospitals, useful for medical-tourism stays
33rd-floor infinity pool with city views draws consistent praise
Weekday evening reception (drinks, light snacks) is a well-regarded touch
Lower rates than the downtown and Sentosa Bonvoy hotels
cons: Further from Marina Bay, Orchard Road, and Sentosa's main attractions
Standard and even premium rooms are described as small
Breakfast is a paid add-on (about SGD 35) unless you hold Titanium Elite or above
research_highlights: The 33rd-floor infinity pool is a consistently praised highlight
The weekday evening reception with drinks and snacks draws specific positive mentions
Direct MRT connectivity is repeatedly cited as a practical advantage
research_watchouts: Rooms are described as small even at premium tiers
Breakfast costs roughly SGD 35 and is only complimentary for Titanium Elite and above
At least one review noted the pool deck was closed for renovation during their stay

faqs.question: Is breakfast included at Courtyard by Marriott Singapore Novena?
faqs.answer: Not for most guests -- breakfast is a paid add-on at roughly SGD 35 per person, and is only complimentary for Marriott Bonvoy Titanium Elite members and above, consistent with the brand's select-service benefit structure.

faqs.question: Is Courtyard by Marriott Singapore Novena connected to the MRT?
faqs.answer: Yes -- the hotel is built directly on top of Novena MRT station, making it one of the most transit-connected Bonvoy properties in this directory's Singapore list.

reviews.title: Hotel Review: Courtyard by Marriott Singapore Novena (Premier Skyline Room)
reviews.author: Mark Chua
reviews.summary: A room-focused review of the Premier Skyline Room, praising the 22sqm layout, big windows and standout skyline views. Notes a Nespresso machine and USB charging, but flags an open bathroom with no door lock and a steep price.

reviews.title: Courtyard by Marriott Novena in Singapore – a Hotel Review
reviews.author: Quirrow
reviews.summary: A New Year stay in a Premier Skyline King above Royal Square mall by Novena MRT. Praises the Sky22 breakfast and rooftop pool with Marina Bay Sands glimpses, but finds the compact rooms overpriced near S$300 a night.

reviews.title: Review: Courtyard By Marriott Hotel Novena (Singapore)
reviews.author: Dania
reviews.summary: Rates it 4/5, highlighting elegant common areas, a rooftop infinity pool, the Las Palmas bar and high-floor views. Rooms are clean but amenities limited; disliked the soft mattress topper, tiny gym and no turndown. Decent value.

reviews.title: Courtyard by Marriott Singapore Novena Review: Sensible City Stay
reviews.author: Rubbish Eat Rubbish Grow Editorial Team
reviews.summary: Frames it as a practical, well-connected pick away from the Orchard crowds. Compact modern rooms with skyline windows and a photogenic rooftop pool are highlights, while Sky22 breakfast is serviceable: clean, comfortable, sensible.
